text: Over the last 30 days, several visitors raised concerns about the food quality at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library, with one critical review highlighting a limited and unappealing menu, including issues with the grilled cheese and potato salad. Wait times were mentioned in three reviews, suggesting some visitors experienced delays. Service and atmosphere received occasional comments, but these were less frequent. Overall, the average rating remains positive at 4.62 out of 5, though food options and preparation appear to need attention.

windows.60: Visitor reviews over the last 60 days indicate ongoing issues with the food service at the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library. Many guests found the menu limited and the food quality below expectations, with complaints about portion sizes, pricing, and preparation. Service delays and long wait times were also noted, particularly related to kitchen backups and restricted ordering options late in the day. While some visitors appreciated aspects of the library itself, the food and dining experience consistently drew criticism and should be addressed.

Many guests found the menu limited, overpriced, and of poor quality, with specific complaints about portion sizes, preparation, and pricing. Service problems included long wait times and inconsistent availability of menu items, leading to frustration. While the library itself receives positive comments, the food and dining experience are areas needing attention to improve visitor satisfaction.
